name: SQL
desc: The gap that costs most people offers. Every topic covered at interview depth — syntax, gotchas, edge cases, and the "why" behind each concept.
tip: If you blank on syntax, narrate your logic out loud — 'I'd partition by department, rank by salary descending, filter where rank = 1.' Interviewers weight reasoning as much as the final query.

r: RANK leaves gaps after ties (1,1,3). DENSE_RANK does not (1,1,2).
WHERE runs before GROUP BY — cannot use aggregates. HAVING runs after.
Re-evaluates for every outer row. Slow on large data.
LEFT JOIN + WHERE on right column
Drops NULLs → becomes INNER JOIN. Move filter to ON clause.
NOT IN returns zero rows if subquery has any NULL. Use NOT EXISTS.
CROSS APPLY can reference outer columns in inner query. JOIN cannot.
Row versioning — readers never block writers. Enable at DB level.
Include all queried columns in the index to avoid Key Lookups.
